newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO calls for world sanctions against Israel.
newsitem.headline: PLO calls for world sanctions against Israel.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority on Saturday called for an emergency meeting of the United Nations General Assembly to impose sanctions against Israel to force it to respect international laws.

"As a result of the freezing of the peace process by Israel, its settlement aggression on Palestinian land and against our people, the Palestinian Authority calls for an immediate emergency meeting of the United Nations General Assembly to impose economic and political sanctions against Israel to compel it to respect international law," said a statement issued early on Saturday after a weekly cabinet meeting.
Israeli-Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) peace moves have been frozen since Israel broke ground on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Three months of deadlock last week erupted into daily clashes between stone-throwing Arab demonstrators and Israeli troops in the divided West Bank city of Hebron.
The Authority condemned Israel for firing on unarmed Palestinians in recent clashes. Some 150 Arabs have been wounded in the unrest.
The Authority warned that patience among the Palestinian public over Jewish settlement on lands occupied by the Jewish state in 1967 was growing thin.

"The arming of Jewish settlers and the protection offered to them by Israeli soldiers while they continuously attack Palestinian landowners will not leave our masses with any choice but to confront this aggression by all available means."
Israel has accused the PLO of orchestrating the unrest.

The violence erupted in Hebron last Saturday after a U.S. congressional vote demanded President Bill Clinton recognise Arab East Jerusalem -- occupied by Israel in 1967 and revered by Palestinians as the capital of their future state -- as part of the capital of the Jewish state.

"The Palestinian Authority condemns and denounces the decision of the American Congress over Jerusalem which is a dangerous and serious violation of international legitimacy and harms United States credibility as co-sponsor of the peace process," the cabinet statement said.

The Authority called on the U.S. administration to pressure Israel to halt settlement activity. "Otherwise the process of peace, security and stability, as well as U.S. interests, will face grave dangers."
